# landscape_LC_control

**AIDA-Scout S1b (landscape scalar cascades), benchmark `L-C`** -- generated by
`landscape/make_processes.py`.

The negative control. At lambda'/lambda = 1e-6 the hidden-sector quartic is switched off, so no scalar can decay into a pair of lighter scalars: the cascade never starts and each of the two scalars from the Higgs decays straight to the Standard Model.

The topology collapses exactly as intended -- **multiplicity goes to exactly 4**, and the flavour composition flips from pion/gluon-dominated to c (54%) and tau (18%), which is an h -> aa -> 4c / 4tau signature this repository already has prompt benchmarks for and existing searches already cover.

It shares L-B's production, coupling and cross section exactly; one parameter separates uncovered from covered.

Reference: R. T. D'Agnolo, M. Ettengruber, L.-T. Wang, *Landscapes at
Colliders*, arXiv:2512.18001. The model is a Python port of the authors' Julia
code; see [`landscape/README.md`](../../landscape/README.md) for the port, its
eight-tier verification, and the deliberate deviations.

## Parameters

| | |
|---|---|
| N (number of singlet scalars) | 200 |
| lambda | 0.0027 |
| lambda' | 2.7e-09 |
| lambda'/lambda | 1e-06 |
| M* | 10000 GeV |
| v2 | 221.4 GeV |
| mixing angle theta | 0.027 |
| mass spectrum | uniform on [0.7071, 10] GeV |
| **spectrum seed** | **424242** (one landscape realisation, fixed across jobs) |
| production | gg -> h -> phi_i phi_j |

## Normalisation

| | |
|---|---|
| cross section x BR | **2.699 pb** |
| BR(h -> BSM), physical (Gamma_SM = 4.1e-3 GeV) | 0.0994 |
| BR(h -> BSM), Julia normalisation (Gamma_bb(pole) x 1.89) | 0.05565 |
| Higgs signal-strength bound | 0.1 -- **within** |

lambda is retuned from the shipped 1e-4 to 0.0027, which is what puts this
point at the Higgs signal-strength bound instead of three orders of magnitude
below it. Gamma(h -> phi phi) goes as lambda^2 and nothing else in the chain
depends on lambda, so the retuning is a closed form -- `landscape/retune.py`.

The bound is applied to the **physical** BR. The Julia normalises to
Gamma_bb(pole) x 1.89 = 8.13e-3 GeV against a true SM width of 4.1e-3, so
tuning its number to 0.1 would land at a physical 0.17, over the bound
(deviation 7d).

lambda' is deliberately **not** scaled with lambda. Every hidden-sector width
carries lambda'^2 and every Standard Model width carries theta^2 ~ lambda^2, so
raising lambda alone reweights hidden against SM -- but the hidden channels
already hold at least 1 - 6.9e-8 of every above-threshold scalar's width at the
shipped point, and a factor 729 in lambda^2 leaves them at 1 - 5.0e-5. The
largest change in hidden fraction anywhere in the spectrum is 5.0e-5, and 400
cascades driven by the same uniform stream come out element-for-element
identical, so multiplicity and flavour composition are unchanged.
`landscape/tests/test_tier8_retune.py` asserts both.


## Lifetimes

```
Lifetimes: L-C
  200 scalars, hidden-pair threshold 2*m_min = 1.549 GeV
  ctau over the whole spectrum: min 2.619e-06  median 1.511e-05  max 5.807e-03 mm
  above threshold (182 scalars, hidden pair channel open): median 1.277e-05 mm  max 2.948e-03 mm
  below threshold (18 scalars = 9.0%, mixing only): median 3.738e-03 mm  max 5.807e-03 mm  <-- DISPLACED
```

The sub-threshold scalars still carry the longest lifetimes, but at this lambda
they are microns, so the sample is prompt for all detector purposes. `L-B-displaced`
is the same topology with the shipped lambda, where the same scalars reach
millimetres.


## Why it evades (or does not evade) the Phase-2 L1 menu

| Seed | Threshold | Fires? |
|---|---|---|
| PuppiHT | 450 (constituents pT > 30) | no -- 2.25% |
| SinglePuppiJet | 230 | no -- 1.65% |
| QuadJet | 400,70,55,40,40 | no -- the 400 GeV HT leg already fails |
| DoubleTkMuon (BPH) | 2,2, abs(eta)<1.5, dR<1.4, OS, dz<1cm | no -- 1.9% |
| DoubleTkMuon (central) | 4,4 | no -- 3.3% |
| DoubleTkElectron | 25,12 | no -- no electrons in the cascade |
| DoubleTkIsoPhoton | 22,12 | no -- the photon channel is below 0.1% |
| DoublePuppiTau | 52,52 | no |
| PuppiETmiss | 200 | no -- nothing escapes but tau neutrinos |


## What is in the LHE

The hidden scalars are written into the record, not just the final partons.
They share one PDG id (9000006) and each carries its own mass and its own
`VTIMUP`, because an LHE has nowhere else to put a per-particle displacement
and the cascade's decay vertices are the physics.

`LesHouches:setLifetime = 1` in the card is load-bearing: it is Pythia's
default, but `= 2` silently discards `VTIMUP` and collapses every hidden-scalar
decay vertex to the origin, making the sample prompt with no error. Verified by
A/B: with `= 1` the scalar decay vertices reach 232 mm; with `= 2` they are all
exactly zero.

Colour is connected **locally**: each phi -> q qbar is its own singlet with one
fresh tag, each phi -> g g its own closed loop with two. Connecting colour
across the cascade would string the whole event together and materially change
the hadronic activity.

## Measured, truth level, 2000 events, no pileup

| | L-B | L-C (this point) |
|---|---|---|
| parton multiplicity, mean | 12.38 | **4.00** |
| parton energy, median | 12.4 GeV | **47.8 GeV** |
| flavour | pi+- 38%, s 18%, g 18%, pi0 18%, mu 8% | **c 54%, tau 18%, g 14%, s 5%, b 4%** |
| charged multiplicity, median | 113 | 113 |
| jets above 30 GeV, median | 2 | 2 |
| HT, median | 121 GeV | 108 GeV |
| hidden-scalar decay r_xy, median / max | 0.00 / 0.40 mm | 0.00 / 0.43 mm |

### The control is now genuinely prompt

At the shipped lambda this point was **not** prompt -- its scalars decayed
through theta^2-suppressed mixing with millimetre lifetimes, so "already
covered by prompt searches" needed qualifying. The retuning fixed that as a
side effect: cutting the lifetimes by 729 puts the hidden-scalar decay vertices
at a median of 0.00 mm and a maximum of 0.43 mm. The control is prompt where it
claims to be.

80% of its *charged* particles still come from beyond 100 um, but that is
ordinary charm and tau lifetime, not the model -- which is exactly what a
prompt h -> aa -> 4c search is built to handle.

### It is still not distinguishable at jet level

HT 108 vs 121 GeV, leading jet 62 vs 67 GeV, charged multiplicity identical.
L-C separates from L-B in **substructure, flavour and multiplicity of the hard
process**, not in trigger-level energy flow. Use it as a control for what the
anomaly detector keys on, not for what the menu sees.

## Downstream limits

* `cards/delphes_card.dat` has **no d0 dependence** in its L1T tracking
  efficiencies -- they are functions of pt and eta only. The sample is correct
  at truth level, but the chain will not reproduce the loss of displaced tracks
  at L1. This matters most for `landscape_LB_higgs_displaced` and
  `landscape_LA_direct`.
* Delphes drops particles produced outside the tracker (R = 1.29 m, half-length
  3 m).
* **L1 menu decision bits are not produced here.** No CMSSW Phase-2 emulator
  exists in this repository; the menu column above is truth-level Pythia against
  the offline thresholds, which is an upper bound on what the real menu sees.

## Running

```bash
apptainer exec --bind $simdir \
  /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch/registry.hub.docker.com/jmduarte/mapyde:latest \
  sh $simdir/run.sh landscape_LC_control <nevents> <seed> $simdir False
```

This point uses the **pythia** branch of `run.sh`, with the landscape LHE
pre-step in front of it. `run.sh` runs `landscape.make_lhe` with the arguments
in `landscape_LC_control_lhe_args.dat`, writes the parton-level summary to
`outdir/parton_level.txt`, and then hands the LHE to the same Pythia -> HepMC
-> PU 200 -> Delphes -> parquet chain every other point uses.

To produce the LHE on its own, outside the job:

```bash
python3 -m landscape.make_lhe --benchmark L-C --fast-branching \
    --nevents 10000 --seed 1234 --out L-C.lhe --fragment L-C.cmnd
```
